title: One answer to what an attempt changed that no task declares, and a committed task always closes
description: In stage 1's a1c the restore point the base's suite parked under .claude/audit-backups/ was left out of the task commit by commit-task-work (it reads _manifest_io.PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE) and then refused by audit-task done's _uncommitted_leftovers, which skips only bookkeeping and run-state paths. Three readers compute the same question with their own skip lists (commit-task-work attempt_refusal, audit-task _uncommitted_leftovers, drive-phase's set-aside split), and a fix to one has twice missed another.
desiredOutcome: The commit step, the close and the writer's set-aside ask one shared function what an attempt changed that no in_progress task declares, so a path the plugin owns is never refused by one of them after another left it out; and a task whose work the drive committed closes on that commit instead of being offered no-change or retry

findings.issue: The close now leaves out every PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE row, including the plugin's own `.claude/audit.config.json` and `.claude/.gitignore`, whether git tracks them or not. A task that edits a TRACKED config without declaring it used to be refused by the close as an undeclared change made during the attempt. It is now named in an informational line and the close goes ahead with that edit left uncommitted. The commit step already did the same (ctw-at7 pins the config as left out), so the two readers agree, which is the point of the task. But the new lo-po cases pin only the restore point; none pins a tracked config edit, so the widening is unexamined.
findings.resolution: Keep the commit and the close in agreement, since exempting only untracked config in the close alone would bring back the divergence this task removes. Add a case in test_audit_task for a tracked `.claude/audit.config.json` edited during the attempt, so the behaviour is pinned either way. If the owner wants a tracked config edit refused, change the table row or the shared function once so both readers follow.

findings.issue: The comment says the scan is 'on what the readers MAY NOT NAME rather than on the instance that was found', and the task asked for the invariant, not the instance. What sc-ua5 does is a name blacklist: plugin_owned_under, PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE, attempt_strays and logs_dir. A reader that hardcodes `.claude/audit-backups`, keeps its own `under_any` list, or imports the table under another alias passes it (an `ImportFrom` alias is not a Name node). sc-ua6 only counts calls to `undeclared_changes`. It does not stop a reader from filtering the result again with a skip list of its own. The comment and docstring promise more than the check delivers.
findings.resolution: Either state the limit in the comment ('names the three primitives that were found; a differently spelled skip list is not seen') or widen the check to something the readers share. For example, assert that each reader has no local `skip`/`bookkeeping` list beyond its documented bookkeeping argument, and that it does not call `status_paths` or `under_any` itself.

findings.issue: The tree-wide scan passes on `outside == []` without counting the files it read. If the `os.walk(_output.SCRIPTS_DIR)` found no `.py` (a wrong anchor, or a skipped directory), the check would read as 'nobody else reads plugin_owned_under' and stay green. That is a filter narrowing to nothing, the shape the repo's no-silent-pass rule names. sc-ua7 shows the per-source scan can fail, but not that this walk reaches files.
findings.resolution: Collect the scanned names and assert the walk reached the home modules (`_manifest_io.py` and `_scoped_commit.py` among the files read) and more than a handful of files. Put the count in the check text so a narrowed walk goes red.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "a commit after the attempt's start head carrying the task's Audit-Row": own_commit takes nonces from every journal row naming the task in ANY attempt (the loop at ~3795 filters on taskId only, not on rows after the current attempt's task.start row), and runs `git rev-list <start>..HEAD` without checking that `start` is an ancestor of HEAD. After a rebase or reset the recorded start head can survive off HEAD's history, `start..HEAD` then lists every commit since the merge base, and a previous attempt's still-reachable carrier is taken as this attempt's commit and closed on. _scoped_commit.attempt_span (_scoped_commit.py ~1234-1262) states it is the ONLY reader of the attempt's span and answers (None, why) for exactly this case; own_commit is a second reader with a different rule, the shape that docstring warns about. Read from the code; not run.
findings.resolution: Do not run rev-list directly: check `git merge-base --is-ancestor <start> HEAD` (non-zero or error returns None, so the caller keeps the no-change decision) or read the span through _scoped_commit.attempt_span, and limit nonces to journal rows after the current attempt's task.start row.

findings.issue: A commit that was later reverted still closes the task. own_commit returns the Audit-Row carrier C without asking whether C's work is still in HEAD; after `git revert C` the carrier is still in start..HEAD, and the done --commit path (which asks whether the attempt changed a declared file in the span) also still sees C change it, so the task is recorded done on a commit whose effect is undone.
findings.resolution: Require that the declared files still differ between C^ and HEAD in C's direction, e.g. no commit in C..HEAD touches the declared files, or `git diff --quiet C HEAD -- <declared>` is false-then-equal to C's own change; otherwise return None so the old decision stands.

findings.issue: The carrier's subject header is not checked. _invariants.recorded_commits (_invariants.py ~784-790) counts a carrier as the scoped commit only when its subject opens with the class header AND the trailer is in the last paragraph, because a squash or any commit that absorbs the message keeps the trailer. own_commit checks only inLast, so a squash-absorbing commit in the range whose last paragraph ends with the trailer is accepted as the task's commit. The task commit's header is commit-task-work.message_parts' `<type>(<taskId>): audit - ...`.
findings.resolution: Also require carrier subject to match the task commit's header shape for this task id (`(<taskId>): ` after the type), treating a non-matching carrier as not found, as recorded_commits does with `absorbed`.

findings.issue: No case pins the range. Mutation: replace `rev-list start..HEAD` with `rev-list HEAD` (drop the range). tcc3's carrier sits after the start head, so it is found either way; no case has a carrier at or before the start head that must be ignored. The task clause is literally 'a commit after the attempt's start head'.
findings.resolution: Add a case where a carrier exists before the attempt's start (a previous attempt's commit, or a start recorded after the commit) and own_commit/next must still answer no-change.

findings.issue: No case pins the `inLast` filter. Mutation: delete `if c["inLast"]` from the `held` set. Every carrier the fixture produces has its trailer in the last paragraph, so the filter never rejects anything.
findings.resolution: Add a case whose range holds a commit with the Audit-Row line in a non-last paragraph and assert it is not closed on.

findings.issue: No case pins the withdrawn-nonce filter. Mutation: delete `nonce not in withdrawn`. The fixture journal has no audit.commit.withdrawn row, so the filter never fires and a withdrawn row's nonce would be accepted with no case red.
findings.resolution: Add a case with a withdrawal row for the task's nonce plus a commit still carrying that trailer, and assert no-change is still offered.

findings.issue: No case pins the `task.get("commit")` guard (and none the status guard). Mutation: drop `or task.get("commit")` from the first line of own_commit. Every close_task call in tcc1-4 has an in_progress task with commit null, so the dropped guard changes no outcome.
findings.resolution: Unit-call own_commit with a task that has a recorded commit and a carrier in range, and assert None.

findings.issue: tcc4 never produces a carrier: the stub returns 'nothing to commit' and no commit-task-work run happens, so there is no Audit-Row row and no carrier commit anywhere, and own_commit returns None at the first 'not carried' exit. It would stay green for the four mutations above together (drop the range, the inLast filter, the withdrawn filter and the commit guard), so it is not the twin that keeps the fix from firing on everything. It also leaves unpinned the unreadable-start-head and unreadable-journal exits, which the docstring promises return None.
findings.resolution: Make the twin a case with a real carrier that must be ignored (before start, withdrawn, or not in the last paragraph) and add the start-head-missing / journal-unreadable cases.

review.outcome: [findings: 11 - 0 high, 2 med, 9 low; 0 with a recorded fix commit]

tasks.title: One function answers which paths an attempt changed that no in_progress task declares, and every reader asks it
tasks.description: Move the question - paths changed during the attempt (by the start snapshot, else mtime against startedAt) that no in_progress task covers, with the plan's bookkeeping, the plugin's run state and every _manifest_io.PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE row taken out and returned separately as named plugin-owned state - into one function in _scoped_commit, and make commit-task-work.py's attempt refusal, audit-task.py's _uncommitted_leftovers (the close) and drive-phase.py's set-aside split call it, deleting their own skip lists. The close then never refuses a path the commit step left out as plugin-owned. Add a case per reader in which a restore point appears under .claude/audit-backups/ during the attempt: the commit leaves it out and names it, and the close on that commit is accepted; and a lint or case that fails when a reader computes the skip list itself (the invariant, not the instance).

Existing pins unchanged and green: ctw-at7/at8 (commit side), xs6 (drive-phase). PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: the attempt_strays sentence rewritten for undeclared_changes and the module-map fence regenerated with tools/lints/_deps.py --write-map (drive-phase gained the _scoped_commit edge; test__deps g1 was red until then). Evidence: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py (whole tree) exit 0, 194/194 files, 17007 cases, after the last edit; tests/test_audit_task.py alone 1108/1108. Tests were written after I had read the implementation (the brief gives the files), so red-first rests on the helper's run against HEAD. Dependants: commit-task-work.py (8 listed readers incl. _invariants, _verdict_binding, commit-manifest-index, run-test-gate, drive-phase) - still correct: its CLI, JSON answer keys (attempt.during/predates/pluginOwned/cleanAtStart), note wording and exit codes are unchanged; only the three helper functions left, and no listed file or test named them (grep of tests/tools/plugins). audit-task.py (96 names used elsewhere) - still correct: only the private _uncommitted_leftovers arity (3 to 4) and _run_state_rels (deleted) changed, grep shows no outside user; one new informational output line on a close that has plugin-owned state. drive-phase.py - changed: new import of _scoped_commit and plugin_owned_paths now delegates (same return, pinned by xs6); the module-map fence in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md changed accordingly. Edited under P137.1 although the brief lists it as last declared by P137.2 (pending); the plan gate did not refuse the write. _scoped_commit.py - changed: attempt_strays removed (only user was commit-task-work; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md named it and was updated), five names added; close-phase, commit-audit-state, commit-manifest-index, _live_copy import it for other names, untouched. tests/test__scoped_commit.py, test_commit_task_work.py, test_audit_task.py, test_drive_phase.py - test_commit_task_work.py and test_drive_phase.py were not edited (their existing ctw-at7/at8 and xs6 cases are the commit and set-aside readers' cases and pass); the other two gained the cases above. Not done: no new case in test_commit_task_work/test_drive_phase beyond the existing ones, since they already carry a restore point under audit-backups for those readers.

tasks.title: A task whose work the drive committed closes on that commit when the close was refused after it
tasks.description: When the drive committed a task's work (a commit after the attempt's start head carrying the task's Audit-Row) and the close was then refused, the next step finds nothing to commit and offers only no-change (which records a false outcome) or retry (which pays a writer to redo committed work). Make the drive recognise that commit and close the task on it - the close re-asked through the same checks, refusing as before when they still refuse - and never offer no-change for a task whose own commit is in the range. Add a case reproducing a1c's sequence: commit lands, close refused, the refusal's cause removed, next step closes on the commit.

add: tests/test_drive_phase.py: after a commit landed and the close was refused, the next step closes the task on that commit and never offers no-change

tasks.title: No suite writes into the real checkout's .claude/, and the sweep names one that does
tasks.description: Stage 1 runs a2 and a1c each found a 524-byte demo-plan restore point (.claude/audit-backups/audit-plan.json.bak-<UTC>) and a .gitignore line appear in the clone's .claude/ during the writer's whole-tree sweep, with no layout verb in any tool call: a suite resolves its project from its own location (REPO_ROOT) instead of its scratch and runs the layout migration's backup against the real checkout. Find the suite (run the sweep over a clean checkout and diff .claude/ before and after; grep tests/ for migrate-manifest, ensure_backup_dir, backup_dir_for and REPO_ROOT used as a project), make it use a scratch project, and extend tools/sweep-selftests.py's watched set to the checkout's own .claude/ so a write there is a finding naming the suite. Red first: the watched-set case fails on the unfixed sweep with a suite that writes there.

add: tools/sweep-selftests.py: a suite that writes under the checkout's .claude/ is a finding naming the suite
